lessons.title: Hello! Introducing Yourself
lessons.grammarTitle: Grammar: The Present Tense of "BE" & Question Structures
grammarFormulae: Affirmative: Subject + BE (am / is / are) + [Info]
canDoSample: Introduce yourself using "My name is..." and "I'm..."
Ask someone's name with "What's your name?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Self-Introduction & Basic Personal Information
commonMistakes: I Rahul.
What your name?
I from India and I live at Mumbai.

lessons.title: Occupations, Workplaces & Indefinite Articles
lessons.grammarTitle: Indefinite Articles (A / An) with Occupations
grammarFormulae: Subject + Verb BE + a/an + Profession
Subject + Verb BE + not + a/an + Profession
Verb BE + Subject + a/an + Profession?
canDoSample: State your occupation using "I am a/an..."
Ask someone's profession with "What do you do?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Occupations, Workplaces & Indefinite Articles (A / An)
commonMistakes: I am doctor.
She is a engineer.
He manager in office.

lessons.title: Family Members, Relationships & Possessives
lessons.grammarTitle: Possessive 's (Genitive) & Possessive Adjectives
grammarFormulae: Name + 's + Family Member + is a/an + Profession
How many + [Plural Family Noun] + do you have?
canDoSample: Name immediate and extended family members in English
Use possessive 's to show relationships (e.g. "David's wife")
lessons.communicativeFunction: Family Members, Relationships & Possessive Forms
commonMistakes: He sister is a doctor.
My mother sister lives in Paris.
They have two childs.

lessons.title: Everyday Objects, Personal Belongings & Demonstratives
lessons.grammarTitle: Demonstratives (This/That/These/Those) & Noun Plural Formation
grammarFormulae: This/That + is + a/an + Singular Noun
These/Those + are + Plural Noun
canDoSample: Name personal, office, and classroom objects in English
Form regular plurals with -s and -es, and identify irregular plurals
lessons.communicativeFunction: Everyday Objects, Personal Belongings & Demonstratives (This / That / These / Those)
commonMistakes: These is my books.
This is a glasses.

lessons.title: Numbers 0–100, Age, Time & Contact Information
lessons.grammarTitle: Age Construction with BE & Number Mechanics
grammarFormulae: Subject + Verb BE + [Number] + (years old)
It is + [Hour] + o'clock / half past + [Hour]
canDoSample: Count and recognize cardinal numbers from 0 to 100 in English
Distinguish tricky pronunciation pairs: -teen vs. -ty (e.g. fifteen vs. fifty)
lessons.communicativeFunction: Numbers 0–100, Age, Time & Contact Information Exchange
commonMistakes: I have 25 years.
I am fifteen (meaning 50).

lessons.title: Colors, Descriptions & Basic Adjectives
grammarFormulae: Pattern 1: [a/an] + [Adjective] + [Noun] | Pattern 2: [Subject] + [am/is/are] + [Adjective]
[Subject] + [BE] + very + [Adjective]
canDoSample: Name 10 common colors and use them to describe personal objects
Use opposite adjective pairs (big/small, new/old, tall/short, hot/cold)
lessons.communicativeFunction: Colors, Physical Traits & Basic Adjectives
commonMistakes: I have a car red.
These are bigs houses.

lessons.title: Places in the City & Prepositions of Location
grammarFormulae: [The + Subject Place] + [is] + [Preposition] + [the + Landmark Place]
Question: Is there a + [Singular Noun] + [Location]? | Answer: Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
canDoSample: Name 12 common urban buildings and public amenities
Use prepositions of place (next to, between, opposite, near, behind, in front of)
lessons.communicativeFunction: City Places, Buildings & Spatial Prepositions
commonMistakes: The bank is next of the hotel.
The hotel is between the bank or the cafe.

lessons.title: Daily Routines & Present Simple (I, You, We, They)
grammarFormulae: [I / You / We / They] + [Base Verb] + [Time / Object]
[Action Verb] + at + [Clock Time]
canDoSample: Describe your complete morning and evening routine in chronological order
Use common daily action verbs (wake up, have breakfast, go to work, eat dinner, sleep)
lessons.communicativeFunction: Daily Routines & Present Simple Affirmative
commonMistakes: I am wake up at 7:00 AM.
I take my breakfast at 8:00.

lessons.title: Present Simple Third-Person Singular (He, She, It)
grammarFormulae: [He / She / It / Singular Name] + [Verb + s/es/ies]
/s/ -> speaks, writes | /z/ -> lives, plays | /ɪz/ -> watches, teaches
canDoSample: Add "-s", "-es", or "-ies" accurately to verbs when subject is he, she, or it
Use irregular third-person forms: have -> has, go -> goes, do -> does
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Others: Third-Person Singular (-s / -es / -ies)
commonMistakes: He live in London and work in a bank.
She haves two brothers.

lessons.title: Days of the Week & Adverbs of Frequency
grammarFormulae: Subject + [always/usually/often/sometimes/never] + Main Verb | Subject + [am/is/are] + [always/usually/often/sometimes/never]
on [Day] | in [the morning/afternoon/evening] | at [Clock Time / night / the weekend]
canDoSample: Name all seven days of the week with accurate pronunciation and capitalization
Use frequency adverbs: always (100%), usually (80%), often (60%), sometimes (50%), rarely (10%), never (0%)
lessons.communicativeFunction: Adverbs of Frequency & Weekly Schedule Patterns
commonMistakes: I go always to the gym on Tuesday.
She always is happy.

lessons.title: Present Simple Negative (Don't / Doesn't)
grammarFormulae: [I / You / We / They] + don't + [Base Verb] | [He / She / It] + doesn't + [Base Verb]
[He / She / It] + doesn't have + [Noun]
canDoSample: Use "don't" + base verb with subjects I, you, we, and they
Use "doesn't" + base verb with subjects he, she, and it (removing the "-s" from main verb)
lessons.communicativeFunction: Negations in the Present Simple
commonMistakes: He doesn't works in a bank.
I not like spicy food.

lessons.title: Present Simple Questions & Short Answers (Do / Does)
grammarFormulae: [Do / Does] + [Subject] + [Base Verb]...? -> Yes, [Subject] do/does. | No, [Subject] don't/doesn't.
[WH- Word] + [do / does] + [Subject] + [Base Verb]...?
canDoSample: Form Yes/No questions with "Do you...?" and "Does he/she...?"
Give natural short answers: "Yes, I do." / "No, I don't." / "Yes, she does." / "No, she doesn't."
lessons.communicativeFunction: Present Simple Yes/No & WH- Questions
commonMistakes: Do you live in Madrid? — Yes, I live.
Where you live?

lessons.title: Food, Drinks & Ordering at a Café (Some / Any / A / An)
grammarFormulae: Countable: a / an + Singular Noun | Uncountable: some + Mass Noun / a cup of / a glass of
Affirmative / Request: some | Negative: don't / doesn't have any | Question: Do you have any...?
canDoSample: Identify and name common foods and drinks (coffee, tea, water, juice, milk, bread, cheese, egg, sandwich, apple)
Distinguish countable nouns (an apple, two sandwiches) from uncountable nouns (water, sugar, bread)
lessons.communicativeFunction: Food & Drink Vocabulary, Countable/Uncountable & Café Ordering
commonMistakes: I want a bread and a water.
I don't have some cheese.

lessons.title: Hobbies, Preferences & Free Time (Like / Love / Hate + -ing)
grammarFormulae: Subject + [like / love / enjoy / hate / prefer] + [Verb-ING] / [Noun]
Subject + prefer + [Noun/Gerund A] + to + [Noun/Gerund B]
canDoSample: Name common hobbies (listening to music, watching movies, playing guitar, swimming, traveling, cooking, taking photos)
Express degrees of preference: love (>90%), like (>70%), enjoy (>70%), don't mind (50%), dislike / don't like (<30%), hate (0%)
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Likes, Dislikes, Hobbies & Verb+-ing Patterns
commonMistakes: I like swim in the summer.
I prefer tea than coffee.

lessons.title: Abilities, Skills & Polite Requests (Can / Can't)
grammarFormulae: Subject + can / can't (cannot) + [Base Verb]
Can + [Subject] + [Base Verb]...? -> Yes, [Subject] can. | No, [Subject] can't.
canDoSample: Express personal physical and intellectual abilities using "I can..." and "I can't..."
Ask others about their abilities: "Can you speak Spanish?", "Can you drive a car?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Modal Verb Can/Can't for Ability, Skill & Polite Requests
commonMistakes: He cans speak German.
Do you can drive?

unitTitle: Unit 2: Home, City Living, Routines & Expanding Horizons

lessons.title: Home & Rooms in the House (There is / There are)
grammarFormulae:
Affirmative: There is + [a/an + Singular Noun] | There are + [Plural Noun]
Negative: There isn't a + [Singular Noun] | There aren't any + [Plural Noun]

Is there a + [Singular Noun]...? -> Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
Are there any + [Plural Noun]...? -> Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
canDoSample: Describe an apartment or house room by room using "There is a..." and "There are two/three..."
Ask about room features and amenities: "Is there a balcony?", "Are there two bathrooms?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Houses, Rooms and Layouts with "There is / There are"
commonMistakes: There is three bedrooms in the house.
In the living room has a sofa.

lessons.title: Furniture, Household Objects & Prepositions of Location
grammarFormulae: [Item] + is/are + [Preposition of Place] + the + [Reference Object]

Where is the + [Singular Noun]? -> It is + [Preposition Phrase]
Where are the + [Plural Noun]? -> They are + [Preposition Phrase]
canDoSample: Locate objects precisely using "next to", "behind", "in front of", "opposite", "above", and "near"
Ask and answer where items are kept: "Where are my keys?" — "They are on top of the desk"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Furniture, Household Objects and Exact Prepositions of Location
commonMistakes: The armchair is in front the window.
The desk is next of the wardrobe.

lessons.title: Morning to Night: Extended Daily Routines & Time Sequencing
grammarFormulae: First, [Action 1]. Then, [Action 2]. After that, [Action 3]. Next, [Action 4]. Finally, [Action 5].
[Subject] + [Present Verb] + at [Time] / in [Part of Day]
vocabSample: get out of bed / get up
take a shower / have a shower
canDoSample: Narrate a complete day using time sequence connectors: "First I wake up, then I take a shower..."
Describe working day schedules: "I arrive at work at 8:30 and check emails"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Morning-to-Night Routines with Discourse Connectors
commonMistakes: After I have breakfast, then I go to work.
Then I am wake up at seven.

lessons.title: Transportation, Commuting & Travel Methods
grammarFormulae:
General Transit: by + [bus / train / car / plane / bike / metro]
Walking: on foot
Specific Vehicle: in + [a taxi / my car] | on + [the 8:00 bus / the train]
[Subject] + take/takes the + [Transit] | [Subject] + drive/walk/ride to + [Location]
canDoSample: Explain how you travel to work, university, or town: "I go by metro", "I commute on foot"
Ask others about commuting routines: "How do you get to the office?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Transportation Methods, Commuting and Prepositions of Transit
commonMistakes: I go to the office by foot.
I travel by my car.

lessons.title: Asking for & Giving Street Directions (Imperatives & Navigation)
grammarFormulae:
[Base Verb] + [Direction / Landmark]
Turn [left / right] | Go [straight ahead] | Cross [the street] | Walk past [the bank]

Excuse me, how do I get to the + [Destination]?
Excuse me, where is the nearest + [Facility]?
vocabSample: go straight ahead / go straight on
cross the street / cross the road
canDoSample: Ask politely for street directions: "Excuse me, how do I get to the central library?"
Give clear turn-by-turn walking or driving instructions using imperatives
lessons.communicativeFunction: Giving and Following Street Directions with Imperatives and Landmarks
commonMistakes: Turn to the left at the bank.
Go to straight for two blocks.

lessons.title: Food, Supermarket Shopping & Countable / Uncountable Nouns
grammarFormulae:
Countable: an apple -> three apples
Uncountable: milk (never *milks*), bread (never *breads*) -> a bottle of milk, two loaves of bread

Affirmative (+): Subject + have/has + some + [plural noun / uncountable]
Negative (-): Subject + don't/doesn't have + any + [plural noun / uncountable]
Question (?): Do you have + any + [plural noun / uncountable]?

How many + [plural countable noun] + do you need?
How much + [uncountable noun] + is there?
How much is/are + [item]?
canDoSample: Distinguish countable foods (apples, eggs, tomatoes) from uncountable foods (milk, bread, rice, cheese)
Use "some" in affirmative statements and "any" in questions and negatives
lessons.communicativeFunction: Food Vocabulary, Supermarket Shopping, and Countable vs. Uncountable Nouns
commonMistakes: I bought two breads and three milks.
How much apples do you want?

lessons.title: Ordering in a Restaurant & Café Conversations
grammarFormulae:
I would like + [Dish / Beverage], please.
Could I / we have + [Item], please?
I will have + [Dish], please.

What do you recommend for [course]?
Does this dish contain [dairy / nuts / meat]?
canDoSample: Order food and drinks politely: "I would like the grilled salmon and a bottle of sparkling water"
Ask the server for recommendations: "What do you recommend for the main course?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Ordering Meals, Politeness Strategies, and Dining Interactions
commonMistakes: I want a coffee and chicken.
Give me the bill.

lessons.title: Clothing, Colors, Sizes & Department Store Shopping
grammarFormulae:
Singular: This + noun (near) | That + noun (far) -> is...
Plural: These + nouns (near) | Those + nouns (far) -> are...

Subject + is / are + too + [Adjective]
It is too big / They are too small
canDoSample: Identify and name basic clothing items and colors with accurate plurals (trousers, shoes, glasses)
Use demonstratives accurately: "this shirt" (near/sing.), "that jacket" (far/sing.), "these shoes" (near/pl.), "those pants" (far/pl.)
lessons.communicativeFunction: Clothing Items, Colors, Fit and Department Store Interactions
commonMistakes: This trousers is too big.
I cannot wear it because it is very small.

lessons.title: Weather, Seasons, Climate & Outdoor Plans
canDoSample: Ask and answer about current weather: "What is the weather like today?" — "It is warm and sunny."
Describe seasonal climate in your country or city: "In summer, it is very hot. In winter, it snows."
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Weather Conditions, Seasons, Temperature and What to Wear
commonMistakes: It is making hot today.
The weather is raining.
What is the weather like in summer? — It likes warm.

lessons.title: Hobbies, Free Time & Expressing Likes & Dislikes
canDoSample: Name 15+ common hobbies, sports, and leisure pursuits in English
Express personal likes, loves, and dislikes using gerund verbs: "I love cooking Italian food", "I don't like jogging"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Leisure Activities, Sports and Expressing Preferences with "like / love / hate + -ing"
commonMistakes: I like play football.
I go play swimming on Sunday.
She plays the yoga in morning.

lessons.title: Abilities, Skills & Permission (Modal "Can / Can't")
grammarFormulae:
Subject + can + [Base Verb]
Subject + cannot / can't + [Base Verb]

Can + Subject + [Base Verb] + ...?
Short Answers: Yes, [Subject] can. / No, [Subject] can't.

Can I / Can we + [Base Verb] + ...?
You can / You can't + [Base Verb]
canDoSample: Express physical abilities and talents using "can": "I can speak two languages", "She can drive a car"
State things you cannot do using "can't": "I can't swim very well", "He can't cook Italian food"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Physical Abilities, Talents, Acquired Skills and Asking Permission with "Can / Can't"
commonMistakes: She cans speak French.
I can to swim very well.
Do you can drive a car?

lessons.title: Health, Physical Sensations & Doctor Visits (Have / Feel)
grammarFormulae:
Subject + have / has + a/an + [Ailment Noun]
Subject + have / has + the flu
Subject + feel / feels + [Adjective]

[Singular Body Part] + hurts
[Plural Body Part] + hurt
canDoSample: Describe health problems using "have a...": "I have a terrible headache", "She has a high fever"
Express physical feelings using "feel...": "I feel dizzy and exhausted today", "I feel much better now"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Illnesses, Aches, Pains, Physical Sensations and Visiting the Doctor
commonMistakes: I am headache.
I have fever today.
I feel myself dizzy.

lessons.title: Past States & Whereabouts (Was / Were)
grammarFormulae: Past Simple of "TO BE": WAS vs. WERE Distribution
Questions with Was / Were: Direct Inversion (No "Did")
Past Time Expressions: Yesterday, Last, Ago, In + Year
vocabSample: last week / last month / last year
canDoSample: Describe past locations and states using was/were: "I was at home yesterday", "They were very happy"
Use negative past forms: "She wasn't at the meeting", "We weren't tired after the trip"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Past States, Locations, Feelings and Whereabouts Using "Was" and "Were"
commonMistakes: Did you were at home yesterday?
We was very tired last night.
I was in Paris since two days.

lessons.title: Past Actions & Stories (Simple Past Verbs)
grammarFormulae: Affirmative Past Simple: Regular Verbs (-ed) & Core Irregular Verbs
Negative Past Simple: Subject + DIDN'T + Bare Infinitive (Base Verb)
Questions with DID: "Did + Subject + Base Verb?"
canDoSample: Narrate completed past actions using regular verbs (-ed): "I worked eight hours yesterday", "She visited her grandmother"
Use high-frequency irregular past verbs: "We went to the beach", "He bought a new laptop", "They had dinner at 8 PM"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Narrating Past Events, Life Stories and Actions Using Regular (-ed) & Core Irregular Verbs
commonMistakes: I didn't went to work yesterday.
Did you saw the new movie?
She buyed a new car last month.

lessons.title: Future Plans & Capstone Review (Be Going To)
grammarFormulae: Structure of "BE GOING TO": Subject + [am/is/are] + going to + Base Verb
Negative & Interrogative with "BE GOING TO"
Unit 2 Capstone Integration: Present, Past & Future Synthesis
vocabSample: next week / next month / next year
canDoSample: Express planned future intentions using "be going to": "I am going to visit my family next weekend", "We are going to start a course"
Form negative future intentions: "He isn't going to work tomorrow", "They aren't going to move"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Future Plans, Intentions & Unit 2 Comprehensive Capstone Mastery
commonMistakes: I am going to visiting my aunt.
She going to buy a new car.
I am go to travel next week.

unitTitle: Unit 3: Daily Connections, Social Plans & Everyday Life

lessons.title: Making, Accepting & Declining Invitations
lessons.grammarTitle: Invitations: Making, Accepting & Politely Declining
grammarFormulae: Would you like + to + [BASE VERB] + Object/Details?
Accept: I'd love to, thank you! | Decline: I'm afraid I can't + [Reason with because / have to]
canDoSample: Extend polite invitations: "Would you like to come to our housewarming dinner?"
Make casual social suggestions: "Let's meet for lunch at the new Italian cafe"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Politely Inviting Others, Proposing Social Activities, Accepting Enthusiastically, and Declining with Courteous Reasons
commonMistakes: Would you like come to my party?
Let's to go to the cafe.
I love to come, thanks.

lessons.title: Appointments, Schedules & Making Reservations
lessons.grammarTitle: Time Prepositions & Booking Modals
grammarFormulae: at + [clock time] / on + [day or date] / in + [the morning / month]
Could I + [make an appointment / reserve a table] + for + [day/time]?
canDoSample: Request an appointment politely: "I'd like to make an appointment for Tuesday morning"
Ask about availability: "Do you have any openings this Friday afternoon?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Booking Appointments, Confirming Time Slots and Rescheduling
commonMistakes: I have an appointment in Monday.
My meeting is on 3:30 PM.
I want reschedule my booking.

lessons.title: Object Pronouns & Giving Gifts or Help (me, you, him, her, it, us, them)
lessons.grammarTitle: Subject vs. Object Pronouns & Double-Object Verbs
grammarFormulae: Subject (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) vs Object (me, you, him, her, it, us, them)
Verb + [indirect object pronoun] + [direct object noun] (e.g., Give me the pen)
canDoSample: Use object pronouns after transitive verbs: "Please help me with this box"
Distinguish subject vs object pronouns: "He sees her" vs "She sees him"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Using Direct & Indirect Object Pronouns to Offer Help and Describe Giving or Sending
commonMistakes: Please help I with my homework.
I saw he at the supermarket yesterday.
Give to me the key.

lessons.title: Possessive Pronouns & Belongings (Whose / mine, yours, ours, theirs)
lessons.grammarTitle: Possessive Adjectives vs. Possessive Pronouns
grammarFormulae: Possessive Adjective + Noun (my bag) vs. Standalone Possessive Pronoun (mine)
Whose + [noun] + is this / are these?
canDoSample: Ask about ownership: "Whose umbrella is this on the chair?"
State ownership using possessive pronouns: "The black jacket is mine, not yours"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Identifying Owners, Asking Whose Items Are These, and Using Possessive Pronouns
commonMistakes: Who's umbrella is this on the desk?
This notebook is my.
That jacket is her's.

lessons.title: Hotel Check-In, Rooms & Guest Services (Facilities & Requests)
lessons.grammarTitle: Hotel Requests & Ordinal Floor Numbers
grammarFormulae: Could I / Could we please have + [noun phrase]?
on the + [first / second / third / fourth / fifth] floor
canDoSample: Complete hotel check-in: "I have a reservation under the name of Carlos Silva"
Ask about hotel facilities: "What time is breakfast served in the morning?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Checking In at a Hotel, Inquiring About Amenities, and Making Polite Guest Requests
commonMistakes: I want check in now.
My room is in the three floor.
Is breakfast include in the price?

lessons.title: Long-Distance Travel & Airport Navigation (Flights, Luggage & Gates)
lessons.grammarTitle: Airport Prepositions & Present Continuous Flight States
grammarFormulae: at + [Gate X / Baggage Claim] / on + [Flight X / the plane] / in + [Terminal X / line]
The flight is + [boarding / departing / arriving / landing]
canDoSample: Check in at the airport counter: "I would like to check in for flight BA 249 to London"
Understand boarding pass details: "Gate 14B, Boarding at 15:45, Seat 22A"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Navigating Airports, Understanding Boarding Passes, Security Checks and Gate Announcements
commonMistakes: The flight departs in Gate 4.
I have two luggages.
I prefer a sit near the window.

lessons.title: Comparing Everyday Things (Comparative Adjectives)
lessons.grammarTitle: Comparative Adjective Rules (Short, Long & Irregular)
grammarFormulae: [Subject A] + is + [Adjective-er] + than + [Subject B]
Subject + is + more + [2+ syllable adjective] + than... OR better/worse than...
canDoSample: Compare sizes and prices: "The train is faster than the bus, but it is more expensive"
Use regular short comparatives: "This room is bigger and brighter than that one"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Forming Comparative Adjectives to Compare Prices, Sizes, Speed, Quality and Preferences
commonMistakes: The car is more fast than the bicycle.
This watch is more better than mine.
My room is bigger that your room.

lessons.title: Superlative Adjectives (The Biggest, The Best, The Most...)
lessons.grammarTitle: Superlative Adjectives (Short, Long & Irregular)
grammarFormulae: Subject + is + the + [adjective]-est + (noun) + in/of [group]
Subject + is + the most + [2+ syllable adjective] / the best / the worst
canDoSample: Describe the top extreme in a group: "Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world"
Use regular short superlatives: "This is the oldest building in our city"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Forming Superlative Adjectives to Describe Extremes in Size, Quality, Speed and Experience
commonMistakes: He is the most fast runner in class.
This is best pizza in the world.
That hotel is the most expensivest.

lessons.title: Talking About the Past (Regular Simple Past Verbs -ed)
lessons.grammarTitle: Regular Simple Past Verbs (-ed) & Past Time Expressions
grammarFormulae: Subject + [Verb-ed] + Object/Details + Past Time Marker
Voiceless sound + /t/ | Voiced sound + /d/ | /t/ or /d/ ending + /ɪd/
canDoSample: Describe finished past events: "I worked for eight hours yesterday"
Use regular -ed past verbs: "We visited our grandparents last weekend"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Finished Past Actions, Routines, and Life Events with Regular Past Verbs (-ed)
commonMistakes: I work yesterday at the store.
She visit me two days before.
We stayied in a nice hotel.

lessons.title: Talking About the Past (High-Frequency Irregular Verbs)
lessons.grammarTitle: Irregular Simple Past Verbs (Common Forms & Patterns)
grammarFormulae: Subject + went / had / bought / took / came + Details + Time Marker
Subject + saw / ate / drank / wrote / spoke / told + Object
canDoSample: Narrate past trips and errands: "I went to the supermarket and bought some fruit"
Express past meals and drinks: "We ate sushi and drank green tea"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Using Common Irregular Past Verbs to Narrate Daily Life, Travel and Shopping Experiences
commonMistakes: I goed to the cinema yesterday.
She buyed a new car last month.
We eated pizza for lunch.

lessons.title: Past Simple Negatives & Questions (did not / didn't, Did you...?)
lessons.grammarTitle: Past Simple Negatives & Question Formations
grammarFormulae: Subject + didn't (did not) + [base verb] + Object/Details
(Question Word) + did + Subject + [base verb] + Details?
canDoSample: Form negative past statements: "I didn't receive your email yesterday"
Ask yes/no past questions: "Did you enjoy the concert last night?"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Forming Past Simple Negative Sentences with "didn't" and Inquiring with "Did you...?" and Wh- Question Words
commonMistakes: I didn't went to work yesterday.
Did you saw the new movie?
Did you like the food? — Yes, I liked.

lessons.title: Expressing Obligations, Needs & Rules (Must, Have to, Need to)
lessons.grammarTitle: Obligations, Prohibitions & Lack of Necessity (Must, Have to, Need to)
grammarFormulae: Subject + must / mustn't + [BASE VERB]
Subject + have/has to + [base verb] | Subject + don't/doesn't have to + [base verb]
vocabSample: don't have to / doesn't have to
canDoSample: State official rules and duties: "You must show your passport at immigration"
Express external obligations: "I have to work on Saturday morning"
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Strong Obligations, General Requirements, Prohibitions and Lack of Obligation
commonMistakes: You must to wear a seatbelt.

[Item / Color / Food] + symbolizes + prosperity / unity / rebirth

I can explain customary dishes, clothing, and rituals associated with traditions.

This tradition symbolize victory of light.
People wear their costume traditional.

lessons.title: Environmental Awareness, Recycling & Sustainable Habits
lessons.grammarTitle: Modal Recommendations & Habitual Actions: "We should / ought to" & "By + V-ing"
grammarFormulae: We should / ought to + recycle / conserve / protect + [Resource]
We can reduce pollution + by taking public transit / by recycling plastic

I can explain simple actions to conserve water and reduce energy consumption.

Plastic takes 400 years to decompose itself.
We should to recycle more paper.

lessons.title: Scientific Discoveries, Space & Natural Phenomena
lessons.grammarTitle: Scientific Facts & Conditionals: Zero Conditional ("When / If + Present, Present")
grammarFormulae: When / If + [Condition in Present Simple], [Result in Present Simple]
[Natural Phenomenon] + causes / creates + [Result]
canDoSample: I can describe planets, stars, and celestial bodies in the solar system.
I can explain cause-and-effect relationships in natural phenomena using zero and first conditionals.

The Mars rover send high photos.
Moon orbit the Earth.

lessons.title: Future Visions, Innovations, Goals & Predictions
lessons.grammarTitle: Future Forecasts & First Conditionals: "Will definitely / probably", "Is likely to", & "If + Present, Will + Verb"
grammarFormulae: Subject + will certainly / will probably / is likely to + [Base Verb]
If + [Condition in Present Simple], Subject + will + [Resulting Action]

I can predict technological trends in AI, autonomous mobility, and green energy.

AI is likely replace human jobs.
I probably will visit Japan next year.

lessons.title: A1 Mastery Milestone, Comprehensive Bridge Review & A2 Transition Synthesis
lessons.grammarTitle: A1 Grand Synthesis: Multi-Tense Cohesion & Discourse Linking
grammarFormulae: [In the past: I started / I learned] + [Now: I can communicate / I practice] + [In the future: I will achieve / I hope to lead]
Although [Challenge], Subject + [Achievement] + because [Reason]

I can negotiate professional, medical, civic, and social situations with high independence.

Although it was hard, but I succeeded.
I am ready to transition on Level A2.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Everyday Encounters, Hobbies, Routines & City Life

lessons.title: Daily Routines, Habits & Frequency Adverbs
lessons.grammarTitle: Adverbs of Frequency & Intensifiers in Present Simple
grammarFormulae: Subject + Frequency Adverb + Main Verb + Complement
Subject + BE (am / is / are) + Frequency Adverb + Adjective/Noun
Subject + Verb + [quite / very / extremely] + Adjective
canDoSample: I can describe my typical daily morning and evening routines in detail.
I can use frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, rarely, never) correctly in sentences.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Daily Habits, Frequency & Personal Routines
commonMistakes: I always am late for work.
She goes often to the gym.
He doesn't never drink tea.

lessons.title: Ongoing Activities vs. Habits (Present Simple vs. Continuous)
lessons.grammarTitle: Present Simple vs. Present Continuous & Stative Verbs
grammarFormulae: Subject + Base Verb (s/es) + Time Marker (usually, every day, generally)
Subject + BE (am / is / are) + Verb-ing + Time Marker (currently, this week, right now)
Subject + Stative Verb (know, understand, believe, need, want, prefer) + Object
canDoSample: I can contrast my permanent job responsibilities with temporary projects.
I can correctly use time markers like "currently", "at the moment", and "usually".
lessons.communicativeFunction: Contrasting Habitual Actions with Ongoing Workplace Tasks
commonMistakes: I am knowing the client very well.
Right now he writes an urgent email.
She is having three meetings today (when meaning possession of a car: She is having a car).

lessons.title: Past Experiences & Completed Events (Past Simple)
lessons.grammarTitle: Past Simple Affirmative, Negative & Question Formation
grammarFormulae: Subject + Past Verb Form (Regular: -ed / Irregular: went, saw, had) + Complement
Subject + did not (didn't) + Base Verb + Complement
Did + Subject + Base Verb + Complement? | WH- + did + Subject + Base Verb?
canDoSample: I can narrate a memorable past experience or vacation in chronological order.
I can use regular (-ed) and common irregular past verbs (went, saw, bought, took, had) accurately.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Recounting Completed Past Events, Trips & Milestones
commonMistakes: I didn't went to the office yesterday.
Where did you stayed last night?
Yesterday I visit my grandparents.

lessons.title: Storytelling & Narrative Sequencing Connectors
lessons.grammarTitle: Narrative Linkers & Sentence Connectors
grammarFormulae: First, [Action 1]. Then, [Action 2]. After that, [Action 3]. Finally, [Resolution].
Clause 1. Suddenly, [Unexpected Event]. | Clause 1; meanwhile, [Parallel Action].
Clause 1 + [and / but / so / because] + Clause 2
canDoSample: I can narrate an unexpected event or travel incident in logical order.
I can use sequence markers (first, then, after that, suddenly, in the end) correctly.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Connecting Events Chronologically with Narrative Markers
commonMistakes: First I wake up then I ate breakfast.
Because it was raining, so we stayed indoors.
At the end, we arrived safely.

lessons.title: Giving Reasons, Causes & Results
lessons.grammarTitle: Cause, Consequence & Concession Connectors
grammarFormulae: Result + because + [Subject + Verb] | Result + because of + [Noun / Noun Phrase]
Cause, so + Result Clause | Cause. Therefore, + Result Clause.
Although + [Contrast Clause], [Main Clause].
canDoSample: I can explain why I made a specific decision or changed my plans.
I can distinguish between "because + clause" and "because of + noun phrase".
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Reasons, Causes, Consequences & Concessions
commonMistakes: Because of he was tired, he went to bed.
Because it was raining, so we postponed the trip.
Although it was difficult, but we finished.

lessons.title: Shopping, Quantities & Transactions
lessons.grammarTitle: Countable vs. Uncountable Nouns & Quantifiers
grammarFormulae: How many + [Plural Countable Noun] + ...? | a few + [Plural Countable Noun]
How much + [Uncountable Noun] + ...? | a little + [Uncountable Noun]
Subject + have + [a lot of / plenty of / enough] + [Countable / Uncountable Noun]
canDoSample: I can ask about quantities and prices using "How much" and "How many".
I can distinguish between countable nouns (apples, bottles) and uncountable nouns (milk, sugar, time).
lessons.communicativeFunction: Managing Quantities, Supermarket Shopping & Transactions
commonMistakes: How much apples did you buy?
I need a few water.
There are many furnitures in the store.

lessons.title: Clothes, Styles & Shopping Comparisons
lessons.grammarTitle: Comparatives, "Too" & "Enough"
grammarFormulae: Short adj + -er + than | more + Long adj + than | irregular (better, worse)
Subject + is + as + [Base Adjective] + as + Object
too + [Adjective] | [Adjective] + enough
canDoSample: I can compare two articles of clothing using regular and irregular comparative adjectives.
I can use "too" and "enough" to describe clothing fit (too tight, not loose enough).
lessons.communicativeFunction: Comparing Clothing Items, Sizes & Personal Styles
commonMistakes: This shirt is more warmer than that one.
These shoes are not enough big.
This dress is as stylish than that one.

lessons.title: Eating Out, Menus & Polite Dining Requests
lessons.grammarTitle: Polite Requests & Modal Verbs in Dining
grammarFormulae: Subject + would like + [Noun Phrase / to + Verb]
Could we + [please] + have + [Noun Phrase]?
Does this contain + [Ingredient]? | Is it possible to make this + [without Ingredient]?
canDoSample: I can place orders using polite structures ("I would like...", "Could we please have...").
I can ask about ingredients, allergens, and vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free options.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Ordering in Restaurants, Asking Dietary Questions & Making Requests
commonMistakes: I want the pasta right now.
Give me the bill.
Is this food have nuts?

lessons.title: Health, Symptoms & Medical Advice
lessons.grammarTitle: Expressing Symptoms & Giving Advice with Should / Shouldn't
grammarFormulae: Subject + have/has + [a headache / a fever / a cough] | Subject + feel/feels + [dizzy / sick / exhausted]
Subject + should / shouldn't + Base Verb + Complement
canDoSample: I can describe common physical ailments (headache, fever, sore throat, cough).
I can explain sensations of discomfort using "feel dizzy / exhausted / nauseous".
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Symptoms, Physical Discomfort & Giving Health Advice
commonMistakes: I am headache.
You should to see a doctor.
He shouldn't to drink cold water.

lessons.title: Future Plans, Intentions & Fixed Arrangements
lessons.grammarTitle: Future with "Be Going To" vs. Present Continuous for Future
grammarFormulae: Subject + BE (am/is/are) + going to + Base Verb + Complement
Subject + BE (am/is/are) + Verb-ing + Future Time Expression
canDoSample: I can express personal future intentions and goals using "be going to + verb".
I can describe scheduled meetings and confirmed trips using the Present Continuous for future.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Future Intentions (be going to) & Fixed Arrangements (Present Continuous)
commonMistakes: I am go to travel to Paris.
Tomorrow I meet my doctor (for fixed appointment).
She is going to starts her new job.

lessons.title: Opinions, Agreement & Polite Disagreement
lessons.grammarTitle: Expressing Opinions, Agreement & Diplomatic Disagreement
grammarFormulae: In my opinion, / I think that / I believe that + Clause (Subject + Verb + Object)
I agree with [Noun / Person] | I see your point, but [Counter-clause]
canDoSample: I can state personal opinions on everyday topics using "In my opinion", "I believe", and "I think".
I can express strong and partial agreement with peers.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Opinions, Stating Beliefs & Nuanced Agreement/Disagreement
commonMistakes: I am agree with you.
I am disagree with this idea.
According to me, the film was boring.

lessons.title: Rules, Obligations & Permissions
lessons.grammarTitle: Modals of Obligation, Prohibition & Permission
grammarFormulae: Subject + must + Base Verb | Subject + have/has to + Base Verb
Mustn't + Base Verb (Forbidden!) vs. Don't have to + Base Verb (Optional/Not necessary)
canDoSample: I can explain workplace, airport, and public safety rules using "must" and "have to".
I can express lack of obligation using "don't have to / doesn't have to".
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Obligations (must/have to), Prohibitions (mustn't) & Permissions (can/allowed to)
commonMistakes: You don't have to smoke in the hospital (when meaning prohibited).
He must to wear a uniform.
She have to work on weekends.

lessons.title: Future Plans, Intentions & Predictions
lessons.grammarTitle: Future Forms: "Be Going To", "Will", and Present Continuous for Arrangements
grammarFormulae: Subject + AM/IS/ARE + going to + Verb (infinitive)
Subject + WILL / WON'T + Verb (infinitive)
Subject + AM/IS/ARE + Verb-ING + Future Time Expression
canDoSample: I can talk about upcoming personal intentions and goals using "be going to".
I can make spontaneous offers, promises, and predictions about the future using "will / won't".
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Future Intentions (be going to), Spontaneous Decisions & Predictions (will), and Fixed Arrangements (Present Continuous)
commonMistakes: I will go to visit my grandma tomorrow (already bought train ticket).
Look at those dark clouds! It will rain right now.
I am promise I will to help you.

lessons.title: Digital Life, Apps & Modern Communication
lessons.grammarTitle: Essential Phrasal Verbs in Technology & Gerund vs Infinitive after Verbs
grammarFormulae: Verb + Particle (+ Object) OR Verb + Object + Particle
Verb + VERB-ING (enjoy, avoid, spend time) OR Verb + TO + VERB (need, forget, decide)
canDoSample: I can describe how I use digital devices and smartphone apps in daily life.
I can use essential tech phrasal verbs (log in, turn on, back up, click on, scroll down) accurately.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Navigating Digital Devices, Software, Apps & Modern Online Communication
commonMistakes: Turn on it, please.
I need update my password.
I enjoy to use this application.

lessons.title: Unit 7 Milestone Review & A2 Communication Mastery
lessons.grammarTitle: Comprehensive Unit 7 Grammar Integration: Modals, Futures, Opinions & Past Narratives
grammarFormulae: MUST (strict rule) vs HAVE TO (external need) vs DON'T HAVE TO (optional) vs MUSTN'T (forbidden)
BE GOING TO (prior plan) vs WILL (spontaneous/promise) vs PRESENT CONTINUOUS (booked appointment)
canDoSample: I can integrate routines, past memories, future plans, and obligations into coherent spoken and written paragraphs.
I can express and defend personal opinions politely using diplomatic formulas.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Cumulative Synthesis: Daily Routines, Opinions, Obligations, Future Plans, Tech Life & Conversational Fluency
commonMistakes: I must to review all my notes tonight.
In my opinion, I am agree with you.
Next year, I will visit Paris (already bought flight tickets).

unitTitle: Unit 8: Workplace Communication, Technology & Social Interactions

lessons.title: Describing People: Appearance, Personality & Character Traits
lessons.grammarTitle: Describing Appearance vs Personality: "Look Like" vs "Look" & Adjective Order
grammarFormulae: Subject + look(s) like + [Determiner] + Noun Phrase
Subject + look(s) + Adjective
Opinion + Size / Physical Quality + Age + Color + Noun
canDoSample: I can describe someone's height, build, facial features, and hair style in detail.
I can describe personality traits such as generous, reliable, outgoing, and easygoing.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Physical Appearance, Personality & Personal Qualities
commonMistakes: He looks like tired today.
She is having blue eyes.
How is your teacher look like?

lessons.title: Relationships, Social Circles & Keeping in Touch
lessons.grammarTitle: Reciprocal Pronouns ("Each Other") & Phrasal Verbs in Relationships
grammarFormulae: Subject (Plural) + Verb + each other (+ Preposition)
Subject + get / gets along (well) with + Object (Person)
Subject + keep in touch (with [person]) / catch up (on [news])
canDoSample: I can describe my friendship circle and how often I see my close friends.
I can use reciprocal phrases with "each other" and "one another" accurately.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Expressing Social Connections, Friendships & Communication Habits

We know ourselves for five years.
I lost the touch with my school friends.

lessons.title: Home & Neighborhood Issues: Describing Problems & Repairs
lessons.grammarTitle: Passive Adjectives, "There is Something Wrong With..." & Need + Gerund
grammarFormulae: There is something wrong with + [Determiner] + Noun Phrase
Subject + BE (is / are) + [broken / clogged / leaking / cracked / stuck]
Subject + need(s) + [Verb-ing / to be + Past Participle]
canDoSample: I can describe household faults such as leaking taps, clogged drains, and broken heating.
I can use passive participle adjectives (broken, cracked, leaking, stained) accurately.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Reporting Household Breakdowns, Faults & Requesting Landlord Repairs
commonMistakes: The water is leaking from the sink, please repair it quickly.
The elevator is broken out of work.
The roof needs to fix.

lessons.title: Travel Experiences & Unforeseen Journey Problems
lessons.grammarTitle: Past Continuous vs Past Simple with "When" & "While"
grammarFormulae: While + Subject + was/were + Verb-ing, Subject + Past Simple
Subject + was/were + Verb-ing + when + Subject + Past Simple
Time Connector + Subject + Past Simple Verb + Complement
canDoSample: I can narrate travel experiences and journey disruptions chronologically.
I can combine Past Continuous (background action) and Past Simple (interrupting event) using "when" and "while".
lessons.communicativeFunction: Narrating Travel Anecdotes, Delays & Managing Journey Disruptions
commonMistakes: While I waited at the gate, the plane was leaving.
I lost my luggages at the airport.
We arrived to London at six o'clock.

lessons.title: Making Recommendations, Suggestions & Giving Friendly Advice
lessons.grammarTitle: Modals for Advice (Should / Shouldn't) & Making Suggestions (Why don't you / How about)
grammarFormulae: Subject + should / shouldn't + Bare Infinitive Verb
Why don't + Subject (you / we) + Bare Infinitive Verb + ?
How about / What about + Verb-ing / Noun + ?
canDoSample: I can recommend local restaurants, museums, and attractions to visitors.
I can give friendly advice using "You should / shouldn't" and "Why don't you...".
lessons.communicativeFunction: Offering Suggestions, Recommending Experiences & Giving Practical Advice
commonMistakes: How about to visit the museum today?
You should to carry an umbrella.
She gave me many good advices.

lessons.title: Customer Service: Polite Complaints, Faulty Items & Returns
lessons.grammarTitle: Polite Requests, Indirect Complaints & Conditional Return Phrases
grammarFormulae: I would like + to-infinitive / Could you please + bare infinitive + ?
I am afraid (that) + Clause (Subject + Verb)
Subject + Verb + because + Clause / due to + Noun Phrase
canDoSample: I can explain that an item is faulty, damaged, or the wrong size.
I can request an exchange or full refund presenting a receipt.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Managing Store Returns, Defective Products & Polite Customer Complaints
commonMistakes: Give me my money back immediately!
I want to change this shirt to a bigger.
The screen is having a scratch.

lessons.title: Workplace Communication: Daily Tasks, Updates & Short Messages
lessons.grammarTitle: Verb + Object + To-Infinitive (Reporting Workplace Instructions) & "Have got to"
grammarFormulae: Subject + asked / told / reminded / advised + Object + to + Base Verb
Subject + have / has got to + Base Verb + Complement
Subject + have/has + Past Participle (for completed) / is/are + Verb-ing (for in progress)
canDoSample: I can write short workplace status updates and emails to coworkers.
I can report instructions and requests using "asked me to [verb]" and "reminded us to [verb]".
lessons.communicativeFunction: Managing Office Communication, Task Delegation & Status Reports
commonMistakes: My boss asked me send the email.
She reminded to me to join the call.
I have got finish the report today.

lessons.title: Appointments, Scheduling & Rescheduling Meetings
lessons.grammarTitle: Polite Inquiries (Would it be possible to...), Time Prepositions (At, On, In) & Phrasal Verbs
grammarFormulae: Would it be possible to + [reschedule / move / change] + Noun + to + Day / Time + ?
at + exact time / on + day/date / in + month/year/duration
Subject + push back (later) / bring forward (earlier) + Object
canDoSample: I can book, reschedule, or cancel a doctor's appointment or business meeting.
I can use polite inquiry structures like "Would it be possible to..." and "Could we reschedule for...".

commonMistakes: I have an appointment in Monday at 3 PM.
Would it be possible to reschedule at next week?
I want to cancel off the appointment.

lessons.title: Education, Courses & Learning Experiences
lessons.grammarTitle: "Used to + Infinitive" (Past Habits & States) vs Present Simple & "Learn how to + Verb"
grammarFormulae: Subject + used to + Base Verb (Affirmative) / didn't use to + Base Verb (Negative)
Subject + learn(s) / learned + how to + Base Verb
Subject + BE (am / is / are) + good at + [Noun / Verb-ing]
canDoSample: I can describe past schooling routines and habits using "used to + infinitive".
I can discuss current learning goals and enrolling in professional or online courses.

I am used to play football when I was young.
She is good in speaking English.

lessons.title: Digital Life, Online Communication & Technical Problems
lessons.grammarTitle: Zero & First Conditionals for Technical Instructions & Real Possibilities
grammarFormulae: If / When + Present Simple, Present Simple
If + Present Simple, Subject + will / won't + Base Verb (or Imperative)
canDoSample: I can describe digital hardware and software problems (freezing, crashing, weak signal).
I can give technical troubleshooting instructions using Zero and First Conditionals ("If you click..., it will...").
lessons.communicativeFunction: Navigating Tech Devices, Online Accounts & Troubleshooting Glitches

My computer was crashed yesterday.
I am out of the battery.

lessons.title: Describing Objects, Materials & Everyday Inventions
lessons.grammarTitle: Passive Voice (Present Simple & Past Simple) for Describing Objects & Inventions
grammarFormulae: Subject + is / are + Past Participle (made / produced / manufactured)
Subject + was / were + Past Participle + by + Agent
It is used for + Verb-ing / It is used to + Base Verb
canDoSample: I can describe what objects are made of (wood, glass, ceramic, stainless steel, recycled plastic).
I can talk about inventions and discoveries using Past Simple Passive ("It was invented in... by...").
lessons.communicativeFunction: Describing Physical Objects, Sustainable Materials & Everyday Inventions

These shoes are make from leather.
The telephone was invented from Alexander Graham Bell.

lessons.title: Health, Minor Illnesses & Pharmacy Advice
lessons.grammarTitle: Health Expressions (Have got a + Ailment), Imperatives & Frequency Prepositions for Dosage
grammarFormulae: Subject + have / has got + a [headache / stomachache / sore throat / fever / cough]
Take + Quantity + every + [Time duration] + [with water / after meals]
Subject (This medicine) + may / might + cause / make + Object

I can ask a pharmacist for over-the-counter medicine for common ailments.

Take this pill before eat.
I am allergic with penicillin.

lessons.title: Life Transitions, Celebrations, Festivals & Milestone Events

Congratulations on + [Noun / Verb-ing] | Wishing you + [Noun Phrase]

I can discuss cultural traditions, festive customs, and seasonal celebrations.

We used to celebrating Diwali together.

Would you mind + Verb-ing | Could we possibly + Base Verb

unitTitle: Unit 9: Life Milestones, Present Perfect & Real-World Fluency

lessons.title: Life Milestones, Growing Up & Personal Background
lessons.grammarTitle: Talking About Past Habits vs Specific Past Events: "Used To" vs Past Simple
grammarFormulae: Subject + used to + Base Verb (+ Object / Time Expression)
Subject + Past Simple Verb + (in + Year / Specific Date)
When + Subject + Past Verb, Subject + Main Past Verb

I can describe major life milestones such as graduating, starting a career, and moving cities.
lessons.communicativeFunction: Narrating Life Stages, Childhood Memories & Life Milestones
commonMistakes: I am used to live in Mumbai when I was young.
Did you used to play football?
I was borned in 1995.

lessons.title: Present Perfect for Life Experiences ("Have you ever...?")
lessons.grammarTitle: Present Perfect for Life Experiences: Form, Function & "Ever / Never"
grammarFormulae: Subject + have / has (+ never) + Past Participle (V3)
Have / Has + Subject + ever + Past Participle...?
Subject + have/has been to [place] vs have/has gone to [place]
canDoSample: I can ask questions about life experiences using "Have you ever + past participle?".
I can state things I have done or have never done in my life.

I have ever traveled to Spain.

lessons.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple (Unspecified vs. Specific Time)

Subject + Past Simple Verb + (yesterday / in 2022 / last year / two days ago)
Present Perfect (General Question) → Past Simple (Follow-up Details: When, Where, How)

I can identify past time markers (yesterday, last month, in 2018, two days ago) that require Past Simple.

I saw that movie three times in my life.

lessons.title: Present Perfect with "Just", "Already", and "Yet"

grammarFormulae: Subject + have / has + just + Past Participle (V3)
